To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the phenolic compounds studied here have a dual role as antioxidants and prooxidants.

(i) the antioxidant properties of phenolic flavonoids are related to the number and position of the hydroxyl groups on the C and/or B rings and to the planarity of the flavonoid skeleton; (ii) the antioxidant properties decrease in the order myricetin > taxifolin = morin > 4-OHCoumarin > 3,4′- dihydroxyflavone; (iii) the antioxidant properties are modulated by the binding of

the phenolic compounds myricetin, 3′-hydroxy-4′-methoxyflavone, morin, taxifolin, and 4-hy-droxy coumarin have the potential to act as both pro- and anti-cancer agents, depending on the presence of Cu2+ ions, which can modulate the antioxidant properties of the phenolic molecules and their DNA binding affinity.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification of the structural features of the flavonoids that are responsible for their antioxidant or prooxidant properties and the mechanism of their interaction with DNA in the presence of copper ions.
the elucidation of structure-activity relationship of phenolic compounds, which can be used in the development of new drugs for the prevention and treatment of cancer.
the identification of the most efficient flavonoid derivatives for use in cancer prevention and therapy, which may be achieved by the development of a rational structure-activity relationship.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the antioxidant and prooxidant properties of the phenolic compound depend on their chemical structure, the presence of Cu ions and the nature of the biological system.
flavonoids with a higher number of hydroxy groups are more prone to prooxidant activity, whereas those with a lower number of hydroxy substituents are less prone to prooxidative activity.

phenolic compounds with higher number of hydroxy-groups and planar structure, such as myricetins, morins and taxifolins, are more prone to form stable copper complexes and thus to induce DNA damage via ROS formation, while the less hydroxylated phenolic compounds such as 4-hydrocumarin, 3,4-dihydroxyflavanone, are less prone to induce DNA damage.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

phenolic compounds can act as prooxidants in the presence of transition metals, but the antioxidant activity of phenolics can be enhanced by the formation of metal complexes, which may be beneficial for the treatment of cancer and other diseases.
the antioxidant and prooxidant properties of polyphenols are not only determined by their chemical structure but also by the type of metal ions and their concentrations.

the antioxidant properties of the studied phenolic compounds are not only related to their redox potential and the ability of their hydroxyl groups to donate hydrogen atoms to ROS but also to the formation of Cu(II)-flavonoid complexes, which may induce DNA damage via the Fenton mechanism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
flavonoids with higher number of hydroxy groups, including 3-hydroxyflavonoids such as myricetins, morins and taxifolins, can act as prooxidants in the presence of cupric ions.
the antioxidant properties of phenolic molecules can be modulated by their redox properties and their ability to chelate metal ions, such as Cu2+.
the phenolic compounds studied herein are not simple antioxidant or prooxidant substances.
